mainTopic: Warming, cooking, and bathing on שבת: oil, water, כלי שני, and bathhouse conduct
overview: This amud opens by tying an earlier harsh statement about bathhouse transgressors to a known תנא. A ברייתא then allows strolling through big-city bathhouses on שבת, and רבא limits this to cities, because small village bathhouses are too hot. Next comes a series of ברייתות about warmth on שבת: warming by a fire before rinsing, a warm towel versus a kettle, and taking the chill off water or oil near a fire. The גמרא asks how the תנא קמא rules on oil, and רבה and רב יוסף read the ברייתא one way while רב נחמן בר יצחק reads it another way. שמואל sets the practical rule that for both oil and water the line is יד סולדת בו, which רחבא defines as heat that would burn a baby's belly. A story about רבי in the bathhouse teaches that oil can be cooked, that warming oil counts as cooking it, and that a כלי שני does not cook. The גמרא explains that רבי could teach there because stopping someone from an איסור is different, and רבינא and רב חסדא are reconciled about cooking in the hot springs of טבריה. The amud ends with רבי זירא's report of רבי אבהו floating in a bath, and the answer to the challenge against it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Matching the previous statement to a known תנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the statement just discussed earlier follows the view of a particular תנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like this תנא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the earlier bathhouse discussion. It shows that the statement just made, which called people who break the bathhouse decree 'transgressors,' matches the view of a תנא in a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא's harsh label for people who break a rabbinic rule could seem surprising. By linking it to a תנא who used the same label, the גמרא shows the statement has a source in earlier tradition. It is a quick closing line, not a new topic.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage from the period of the משנה and ברייתא
Like this one; in line with

phrases.english: Like this Tanna:
phrases.notes: Refers back to the ברייתא cited earlier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion earlier by naming its tannaitic source.
steps.raayaObject: The earlier statement that people who break the bathhouse decree are called transgressors
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which a תנא uses the same harsh description

steps.title: Strolling through city bathhouses is allowed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that one may walk through the bathhouses of large cities on שבת without worrying, even if he sweats.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the bathhouses of big cities, a person may stroll through them and need not be concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא saying that walking through a big-city bathhouse on שבת is fine. The person does not have to worry that he is breaking the decree against sweating in a bathhouse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים banned sweating in a bathhouse on שבת. This ברייתא says that simply passing through a large city bathhouse is not covered by that ban. It does not count as using the bathhouse.

phrases.english: Bathhouses of the big cities,
one may stroll in them and need not be concerned.
phrases.notes: He need not worry even if he sweats a little while passing through.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמְבַּטְיָאוֹת שֶׁל כְּרַכִּים מְטַיֵּיל בָּהֶן וְאֵינוֹ חוֹשֵׁשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ruling on a related bathhouse issue.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may stroll through a large-city bathhouse on שבת without concern.

steps.title: רבא limits the rule to cities, not villages
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the permission applies only to city bathhouses and not to village bathhouses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is only true of cities, but village bathhouses, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא narrows the ברייתא. Walking through a bathhouse is allowed only in a city, not in a village.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said 'cities,' and רבא tells us that word was chosen on purpose. Village bathhouses are not included in the permission. The reason is given in the next steps.

phrases.english: Rava said: Specifically cities,
but those of villages, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the ruling of the ברייתא in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Strolling through a bathhouse is allowed only in a city, not in a village.

steps.title: Why the difference between cities and villages?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבא's distinction.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a village bathhouse should be different from a city one. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bathhouse is a bathhouse, so the difference needs a reason. The גמרא wants the logic before accepting the distinction.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רבא's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is a village bathhouse treated differently from a city bathhouse?

steps.title: Small village bathhouses are much hotter
steps.stepSummary: Village bathhouses are small, so their heat is strong, and even walking through them makes a person sweat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since they are small, their heat is great.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a small bathhouse holds its heat. Even walking through it will surely make you sweat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a big city bathhouse the heat spreads out, so passing through it does not really mean sweating. In a small village bathhouse the steam is packed in, so walking through it is the same as sweating there. That falls under the decree.

phrases.english: Since they are small, their heat is great.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Small bathhouses trap strong heat, so walking through them surely causes sweating.
steps.whatToRemember: City bathhouse: you may walk through. Village bathhouse: you may not, because its small size makes the heat strong.

steps.title: Warm by the fire first, then rinse, not the other way
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא allows warming oneself by a fire and then rinsing in cold water, but forbids rinsing first and then warming by the fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A person may warm himself in front of a fire, then go out and rinse in cold water. But he may not rinse in cold water and then warm himself in front of the fire, because he warms the water that is on him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא about warming oneself on שבת. The order matters: warming first and then rinsing is fine, but rinsing first and then warming is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you are wet and stand by the fire, the water on your skin gets warmed. That is like heating water on שבת and washing with it. Warming a dry body first and then rinsing in cold water involves no heated water at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; introduces a ברייתא

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִתְחַמֵּם אָדָם כְּנֶגֶד הַמְּדוּרָה
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: A person may warm himself opposite a fire
and go out and rinse in cold water,
as long as he does not rinse in cold water
and then warm himself opposite the fire,
because he warms the water that is on him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִתְחַמֵּם אָדָם כְּנֶגֶד הַמְּדוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from bathhouses to other cases of warming oneself on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Warming by a fire and then rinsing in cold water is allowed. Rinsing first and then warming is forbidden, because it heats the water on the body.
steps.confusionAlert: Both orders use the same two actions. The only difference is whether wet skin is held up to the fire.

steps.title: A warm towel on the stomach is fine, but a kettle is not
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא allows putting a heated towel on one's stomach on שבת, but not a kettle of hot water. The kettle is forbidden even on a weekday because it is dangerous.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A person may heat a towel and put it on his stomach on שבת. But he may not bring a kettle of hot water and put it on his stomach on שבת. This is forbidden even on a weekday, because of the danger.
steps.whatsHappening: Another ברייתא allows a warm towel for stomach pain on שבת. Putting a kettle of hot water on the stomach is not allowed, and the ברייתא adds that this is forbidden even during the week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dry, warm towel causes no problem. A kettle of water may spill. According to תוספות, the worry is that he will then come to wring out the wet cloth, which is forbidden on שבת. Separately, hot water spilling on the body can burn a person, so it is banned every day for safety.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: A person may heat a towel
and place it on his stomach on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יָבִיא קוֹמְקוּמוֹס שֶׁל מַיִם חַמִּין
phrases.english: as long as he does not bring a kettle of hot water
and place it on his stomach on Shabbat.
And this is forbidden even on a weekday,
because of the danger.
phrases.notes: The hot water could spill and burn him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ברייתא in the same series about warmth on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A heated towel on the stomach is allowed on שבת. A kettle of hot water is forbidden, and it is also forbidden on weekdays for safety.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that one ruling can rest on two separate reasons: a שבת concern and a safety concern.

steps.title: Placing water near a fire only to take off the chill
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא allows putting a jug of water near a fire on שבת. The goal must be only to take away its coldness, not to make it hot.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A person may bring a jug of water and put it in front of the fire, not so it gets hot, but so its coldness goes away.
steps.whatsHappening: This ברייתא allows putting cold water near a fire on שבת. It is allowed only to take the chill off, not to heat the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Heating water until it is hot counts as cooking, which is forbidden on שבת. Making cold water slightly less cold is allowed. The line is between 'hot' and 'no longer cold.'

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מֵבִיא אָדָם קִיתוֹן מַיִם
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: A person may bring a jug of water
and place it opposite the fire.
Not so that it becomes hot,
but so that its coldness goes away.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מֵבִיא אָדָם קִיתוֹן מַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from warming the body to warming water near a fire.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may place water near a fire on שבת to take away its chill, but not to make it hot.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: oil may be warmed near a fire
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says a woman may put a flask of oil near a fire, not to cook it, but only to make it lukewarm.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: A woman may bring a flask of oil and put it in front of the fire, not so it cooks, but so it becomes lukewarm.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה applies the same idea to oil. A woman may put oil near the fire as long as she only makes it lukewarm and does not cook it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like the water in the previous step, the line is between cooking and slight warming. The wording 'not so it cooks' assumes that oil can be cooked. The גמרא will look at this point later.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
A woman may bring a flask of oil
and place it opposite the fire.
Not so that it cooks,
but so that it becomes lukewarm.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מְבִיאָה אִשָּׁה פַּךְ שֶׁל שֶׁמֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the water principle of step 8 to oil.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman may warm oil near a fire on שבת until it is lukewarm, but not cook it.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: warming oil on one's hand
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says a woman may put oil on her hand, warm it by the fire, and rub it on her small son without worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: A woman may put oil on her hand, warm it in front of the fire, and rub it on her young son, and she need not be concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives a different method. The woman warms the oil while it is on her hand, not in a flask, and then rubs it on her child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Warming oil on the hand is a gentle, indirect method. It is not the normal way of heating oil, but is done כלאחר יד, in an unusual way. That is why she 'need not be concerned' about breaking שבת.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
A woman may smear her hand with oil
and warm it opposite the fire,
and smear it on her young son,
and she need not be concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: אִשָּׁה סָכָה יָדָהּ שֶׁמֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different approach to warming oil than רבי יהודה's flask method.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Warming oil on one's hand by the fire to rub on a child is allowed without concern.
steps.whatToRemember: Through all these ברייתות, taking the chill off is allowed, but real heating or cooking is not. רבי יהודה allows a flask of oil to become lukewarm. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל describes warming the oil on the hand.

steps.title: What does the first opinion hold about oil?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the תנא קמא rules about warming oil by the fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: what is the law of oil according to the תנא קמא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about the ברייתא from the steps before. It is setting up a disagreement that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא allowed taking the chill off water near a fire, but he said nothing clear about oil. רבי יהודה and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל did speak about oil. So we need to know whether the תנא קמא is more lenient or more strict about oil.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the scholars
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
Oil, what is it according to the first Tanna?
phrases.notes: Is warming oil permitted or forbidden in his view?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the unstated view of the תנא קמא in the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the תנא קמא permits or forbids warming oil near a fire.

steps.title: Two answers: permitted or forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף say the תנא קמא permits it. רב נחמן בר יצחק says he forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both say: to permit. רב נחמן בר יצחק says: to forbid.
steps.whatsHappening: Two answers are given in short form. Each one will be explained right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is only the headline of the dispute. The next steps show how each side reads all three opinions in the ברייתא so that they fit its view of the תנא קמא.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ לְהֶתֵּירָא,
phrases.english: Rabbah and Rav Yosef, who both say: to permit;

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר לְאִיסּוּרָא.
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: to forbid.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ לְהֶתֵּירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two opposite answers to the question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבה and רב יוסף: permitted. רב נחמן בר יצחק: forbidden.

steps.title: רבה and רב יוסף: oil cannot be 'cooked'
steps.stepSummary: In the lenient reading, the תנא קמא allows oil even when it is very hot, because he holds there is no בישול for oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף, who both say 'to permit': oil, even if the hand pulls back from it, is permitted. The תנא קמא holds there is no cooking for oil.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה and רב יוסף explain their lenient view of the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oil must get extremely hot before it counts as 'cooked'. So for the תנא קמא, even oil at יד סולדת בו heat is not cooked, and warming it is fully allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Hot enough that the hand pulls back from it
Cooking, one of the forbidden מלאכות of שבת

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ לְהֶתֵּירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbah and Rav Yosef, who both say 'to permit':

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמֶן אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַיָּד סוֹלֶדֶת בּוֹ — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: Oil, even though the hand recoils from it, is permitted.
The first Tanna holds
there is no cooking prohibition with oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ לְהֶתֵּירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the lenient answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, oil has no בישול, so warming it is permitted even at יד סולדת בו.

steps.title: רבה and רב יוסף: how the other two opinions fit
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה adds that oil can be cooked, but warming is not cooking. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds that even warming is cooking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה came to say: oil can be cooked, but warming it is not its cooking. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל came to say: oil can be cooked, and warming it is its cooking.
steps.whatsHappening: Still in the lenient reading, the גמרא shows that each later opinion is stricter than the one before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה is stricter than the תנא קמא because he holds oil can be cooked, so he only allows making it lukewarm. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is stricter still: even warming counts as בישול. That is why he only allowed the special case of warming oil on a hand.

keyTerms.meaning: And he came to say (adds a new point)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda came to say
oil is subject to cooking,
but warming it is not its cooking.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲתָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לְמֵימַר
phrases.english: And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel came to say
oil is subject to cooking,
and warming it is its cooking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the lenient reading by explaining רבי יהודה and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a ladder of opinions: the תנא קמא says oil has no בישול; רבי יהודה says it has בישול but warming is fine; רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says warming is בישול.
steps.whatToRemember: In רבה and רב יוסף's reading, each opinion is stricter than the one before it.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: the first opinion forbids even warming
steps.stepSummary: In the strict reading, the תנא קמא forbids warming oil even below יד סולדת בו, because warming is בישול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said 'to forbid': oil, even if the hand does not recoil from it, is forbidden. He holds oil can be cooked, and warming it is its cooking.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains his strict view of the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, the תנא קמא only allowed taking the chill off water. Oil is different: even making it lukewarm counts as בישול, so it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Not hot enough for the hand to pull back

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר לְאִיסּוּרָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said 'to forbid':

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמֶן אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין הַיָּד סוֹלֶדֶת בּוֹ — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: Oil, even though the hand does not recoil from it, is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבַר שֶׁמֶן יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם בִּשּׁוּל,
phrases.english: He holds oil is subject to cooking,
and warming it is its cooking.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר לְאִיסּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite reading of the תנא קמא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, warming oil is בישול and is forbidden even below יד סולדת בו.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: how the other two opinions fit
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה is lenient: warming is not cooking. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל goes back to the strict view: warming is cooking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה came to say: warming it is not its cooking. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל came to say: oil can be cooked, and warming it is its cooking.
steps.whatsHappening: In the strict reading, רבי יהודה argues and is more lenient. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל then argues back against רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the order is not a ladder getting stricter. רבי יהודה permits making oil lukewarm, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees with him and holds like the strict view. This makes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל sound the same as the תנא קמא, which leads to the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: This does not count as cooking it

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda came to say
warming it is not its cooking.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲתָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לְמֵימַר
phrases.english: And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel came to say
oil is subject to cooking,
and warming it is its cooking.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲתָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְמֵימַר הֶפְשֵׁרוֹ לֹא זֶהוּ בִּשּׁוּלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the strict reading of all three opinions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה permits making oil lukewarm. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that warming is בישול.

steps.title: Isn't רבן שמעון בן גמליאל just the first opinion?
steps.stepSummary: In רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל seems to say the same thing as the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is the same as the תנא קמא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading: two opinions in one ברייתא should not say the exact same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both hold that oil has בישול and that warming is בישול. If so, why would the ברייתא list רבן שמעון בן גמליאל as a separate opinion?

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
is the same as the first Tanna?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the strict reading because it makes two opinions identical.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two named opinions in a ברייתא should not be the same. In this reading, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and the תנא קמא agree completely.

steps.title: The difference: doing it in an unusual way
steps.stepSummary: They differ about warming oil כלאחר יד, meaning in an unusual way, like on one's hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: doing it in a backhanded way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two opinions really are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא forbids warming oil in every way. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows it when it is done in an unusual way, like warming oil on one's hand to rub on a child. That is exactly the case he spoke about.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

phrases.english: There is a difference between them:
in a backhanded manner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by finding a practical difference.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical difference (נפקא מינה) between the opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and the תנא קמא seem identical.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both hold warming oil is בישול, but רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permits it when done כלאחר יד.
steps.confusionAlert: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does not say warming oil is not בישול. He agrees it is, but he allows it as an exception when it is done in an unusual way.

steps.title: שמואל's rule: oil and water alike, יד סולדת בו is the line
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that oil and water are the same: heating to יד סולדת בו is forbidden, and below that is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: Oil and water are the same. If the hand recoils from it, it is forbidden. If the hand does not recoil from it, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: Now we get a practical rule from שמואל, which settles how to act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל does not treat oil differently from water. The only question is temperature: below יד סולדת בו is fine, and at that heat or above is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that, treated the same

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
phrases.notes: This is רב יהודה, the student of שמואל.

phrases.english: Both oil and water:
if the hand recoils from it, it is forbidden;
if the hand does not recoil from it, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the opinions to a practical rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For both oil and water, heating to יד סולדת בו is forbidden, and below that is permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: יד סולדת בו becomes the standard measure for בישול in הלכה.

steps.title: What counts as 'the hand recoils'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how hot יד סולדת בו is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the case of 'the hand recoils from it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a clear definition of שמואל's measure. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People's hands feel heat differently, so 'the hand pulls back' needs a fixed standard.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How is it defined?

phrases.english: And what is the case of
'the hand recoils from it'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of the term שמואל used.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact heat level of יד סולדת בו.

steps.title: רחבא: hot enough to burn a baby's stomach
steps.stepSummary: רחבא defines יד סולדת בו as heat that would burn a baby's stomach.
steps.simpleTranslation: רחבא said: Anything that would burn a baby's stomach.
steps.whatsHappening: רחבא answers the question with a clear standard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A baby's belly is very sensitive. That gives a single measure that does not depend on how tough an adult's hand is.

phrases.english: Rachava said:
Anything from which a baby's stomach would be burned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the definitional question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יד סולדת בו means heat that would burn a baby's stomach.
steps.whatToRemember: The practical rule: oil and water are the same, and the line is יד סולדת בו, which means hot enough to burn a baby's belly.

steps.title: Story: רבי in the bathhouse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי tells that רבי did not let him put oil straight into the hot bath. רבי told him to use a כלי שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי said: Once I went in after רבי to the bathhouse, and I wanted to put a jug of oil in the bath for him. He said to me: Take some water in a כלי שני and put it there.
steps.whatsHappening: A story is told about how רבי handled warming oil on שבת. The lessons are drawn in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bath water was hot, and putting the oil into it would heat the oil. רבי insisted on moving hot water into a separate vessel first, and only then placing the oil in it.

keyTerms.meaning: A second vessel (hot food or liquid poured out of the vessel it was heated in)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Avdimi said:
Once I entered
after Rebbi into the bathhouse,
and I wanted to place for him
a jug of oil in the bath,
and he said to me:
Take some in a second vessel and put it there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי: פַּעַם אַחַת נִכְנַסְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story that shows how to act with oil.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Oil should not be put directly into hot bath water on שבת. It may be placed in a כלי שני.

steps.title: Three lessons from רבי's instruction
steps.stepSummary: From the story we learn three things: oil has בישול, a כלי שני does not cook, and warming oil counts as cooking it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn three things from this: learn that oil is subject to cooking; learn that a second vessel does not cook; and learn that warming it is its cooking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws three הלכות from רבי's instruction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי forbade the direct bath, oil must have בישול. Since he allowed the כלי שני, a כלי שני must not cook. Since he was careful even though the oil would only get warm, warming oil itself must count as בישול.

phrases.english: Learn from this three things:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ שֶׁמֶן יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם בִּשּׁוּל,
phrases.english: learn from it that oil is subject to cooking;

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ כְּלִי שֵׁנִי אֵינוֹ מְבַשֵּׁל,
phrases.english: and learn from it that a second vessel does not cook;
and learn from it that warming it is its cooking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lessons from the story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Oil has בישול, warming oil counts as בישול, and a כלי שני does not cook.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that כלי שני אינו מבשל is a basic principle of the laws of בישול on שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: Three lessons: oil can be cooked, warming oil is cooking, and a כלי שני does not cook.

steps.title: How could רבי teach Torah inside a bathhouse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי's behavior. רבי יוחנן says it is forbidden to even think Torah thoughts in a bathhouse.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did רבי do this? But רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: In every place it is permitted to think about Torah, except in a bathhouse and a bathroom!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised by the story in Step 22. רבי taught a הלכה about oil while he was inside the bathhouse, and that seems forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's rule says Torah may not even be thought about in a bathhouse. Speaking Torah out loud there is surely worse. So רבי's instruction to use a כלי שני seems to break this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: To think about (Torah) in one's mind
How did he do this? (a challenge to someone's behavior)

phrases.english: How did he do this?
But didn't Rabba bar bar Chana say
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
In every place it is permitted to think about Torah
except in the bathhouse and the bathroom!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the behavior in רבי's story from Step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's teaching of a הלכה inside the bathhouse
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן forbids even thinking Torah in a bathhouse, so teaching it out loud there should be forbidden.

steps.title: Rejecting the idea that רבי spoke in a non-holy language
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי taught in a secular language. It rejects this using אביי's rule that holy matters may not be said in the bathhouse in any language.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that רבי told him in a secular language, but אביי said: Secular matters may be said in the holy language, but holy matters may not be said in a secular language!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible way out, that רבי spoke in a regular language and not in לשון הקודש. It shuts this down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי teaches that in a bathhouse, what matters is the content and not the language. Torah content stays holy even when it is said in a secular language, so it is still forbidden there. The question from Step 24 is therefore still standing.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (the גמרא raises a possible answer)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read אביי as saying the language decides. In the bathhouse, the content decides: holy content is forbidden in any language, and everyday content is fine even in Hebrew.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא בִּלְשׁוֹן חוֹל אֲמַר לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: And if you say he told him in a secular language,
but didn't Abaye say:
Secular matters
are permitted to be said in the holy language,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל קוֹדֶשׁ אָסוּר לְאוֹמְרָן בִּלְשׁוֹן חוֹל!
phrases.english: but holy matters are forbidden to be said in a secular language!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא בִּלְשׁוֹן חוֹל אֲמַר לֵיהּ, וְהָאָמַר אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks a possible answer to the challenge in Step 24
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggested answer that רבי spoke in a secular language
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי rules that holy content is forbidden in the bathhouse in any language, so the language change does not help.

steps.title: Stopping someone from sinning is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי was allowed to speak because he was stopping his student from doing an איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Stopping someone from doing a forbidden act is different.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the answer to the question from Steps 24 and 25. The rule against Torah talk in a bathhouse does not apply when you are stopping someone from sinning right now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of רבי יוחנן and אביי stays true in general. There is an exception: if someone is about to do an איסור, you may tell him the הלכה even in the bathhouse. רבי's student was about to cook oil on שבת, so רבי was allowed to warn him.

keyTerms.meaning: Separating (stopping) a person from a prohibition

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a lasting הלכה: you may warn someone about an איסור even in a place where Torah talk is normally forbidden.

phrases.english: Preventing someone from a prohibition is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Steps 24 and 25
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Torah may never be spoken in a bathhouse, in any language.
steps.terutzMaskana: To stop someone from an איסור, one may tell him the הלכה even in a bathhouse.

steps.title: Proof from רבי מאיר's student in the bathhouse
steps.stepSummary: A story about רבי מאיר proves that one may teach הלכה in a bathhouse to stop someone from an איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Know that this is true. רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: There was a story with a student of רבי מאיר who went after him into the bathhouse and wanted to rinse the floor. רבי מאיר said to him: We do not rinse. The student asked to smear the floor with oil. He said to him: We do not smear. So we see that stopping someone from an איסור is different. Here too, with רבי, stopping someone from an איסור is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof for the answer in Step 26. רבי מאיר also taught הלכה inside a bathhouse to stop his student from doing something forbidden on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rinsing or oiling the floor on שבת is forbidden, so רבי מאיר spoke up even though they were in the bathhouse. This shows that a great תנא allowed this when it was needed to stop an איסור. The גמרא then applies the same idea to רבי's story.

keyTerms.meaning: Know (this is true); introduces a supporting proof

steps.whatToRemember: Teaching הלכה in a bathhouse is normally forbidden, but it is allowed in order to stop someone from an איסור. We see this from both רבי and רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: Know that this is so,
for Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
There was an incident with a student of Rabbi Meir
who went in after him into the bathhouse
and wanted to rinse the floor.
He said to him: One may not rinse.
The student asked: May I smear the floor with oil?
He said to him: One may not smear.
So we see that preventing someone from a prohibition is different,
and here too, preventing someone from a prohibition is different.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּדַּע, דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer from Step 26 with a story
steps.raayaObject: The rule that stopping someone from an איסור permits teaching in a bathhouse
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: the story of רבי מאיר and his student in the bathhouse

steps.title: רבינא: cooking in the hot springs of טבריה on שבת makes one חייב
steps.stepSummary: רבינא learns from רבי's story that cooking in the natural hot springs of טבריה on שבת makes one חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Learn from this that someone who cooks in the hot springs of טבריה on שבת is חייב. This is because רבי's story happened after the decree, and still he said: Take the water in a כלי שני and put the oil in.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא draws a new הלכה from רבי's story. Since the story happened after the חכמים banned hot baths, the bath must have been the natural springs of טבריה, and רבי still did not allow putting oil straight in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water heated by fire was no longer used for bathing after the decree, so רבי's bath must have been from טבריה springs, which are heated naturally. Even so, רבי worried that putting oil straight into the bath would be cooking. So cooking with טבריה water counts as בישול.

keyTerms.meaning: The natural hot springs of Tiberias
A rabbinic decree (here, the ban on bathing in hot water on שבת)

phrases.english: Ravina said: Learn from this
that one who cooks in the hot springs of Tiberias on Shabbat is liable.

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא מַעֲשֶׂה דְּרַבִּי לְאַחַר גְּזֵירָה הֲוָה,
phrases.english: For the incident with Rebbi happened after the decree,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ: טוֹל בִּכְלִי שֵׁנִי וְתֵן.
phrases.english: and he told him: Take it in a secondary vessel and put it in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי's story and draws a new הלכה from it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cooking in the hot springs of טבריה on שבת makes one חייב.

steps.title: רב חסדא says cooking in טבריה springs is פטור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבינא with רב חסדא's ruling that one who cooks in טבריה springs on שבת is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב חסדא said: One who cooks in the hot springs of טבריה on שבת is פטור!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבינא's ruling. רב חסדא says the exact opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא holds that cooking in naturally heated water is not the תורה's מלאכה of cooking, which is cooking with fire. That seems to clash directly with רבינא's word חייב.

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't Rav Chisda say:
One who cooks in the hot springs of Tiberias on Shabbat is exempt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבינא's ruling from Step 28
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's ruling that cooking in טבריה springs makes one חייב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא rules פטור for the very same case.

steps.title: רבינא's חייב means rabbinic lashes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבינא's חייב means מכת מרדות, rabbinic lashes, and not a punishment from the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does the חייב that רבינא said mean? Lashes for rebelliousness (מכת מרדות).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the clash between רבינא and רב חסדא. Both are right: it is not a תורה-level sin, but the חכמים punish it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's פטור means no תורה punishment such as a קרבן חטאת. רבינא's חייב means the person gets rabbinic lashes because he broke a rule of the חכמים. So the two statements do not argue.

keyTerms.meaning: Rabbinic lashes for breaking a rule of the חכמים

steps.confusionAlert: חייב does not always mean a תורה-level punishment. Here it means only rabbinic lashes.
steps.whatToRemember: Cooking in טבריה springs on שבת is פטור from a תורה punishment, but it is forbidden by the חכמים and gets מכת מרדות.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of the "liable" that he said?
Lashes for rebelliousness (rabbinic lashes).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 29
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבינא meant a תורה-level חיוב, which contradicts רב חסדא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבינא meant מכת מרדות, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: רבי זירא saw רבי אבהו floating in a bath
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא reports that he saw רבי אבהו floating in a bath on שבת. He did not know if רבי אבהו lifted his feet off the floor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: I saw רבי אבהו floating in a bath, and I do not know whether he lifted his feet or did not lift them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins about floating or swimming in water on שבת. רבי זירא describes what he saw and says he is unsure of one detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lifting the feet off the floor (עקר) means actually swimming. Standing with the feet down while bobbing in the water is different. רבי זירא could not tell which one רבי אבהו did.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: אֲנָא חֲזִיתֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: I saw Rabbi Abbahu
floating in a bath,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא יָדַעְנָא אִי עֲקַר אִי לָא עֲקַר.
phrases.english: and I do not know whether he lifted his feet or did not lift them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: אֲנָא חֲזִיתֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new related topic about bathing on שבת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אבהו floated in a bath. Whether he lifted his feet is unknown.

steps.title: Obviously he did not lift his feet, since a ברייתא forbids floating
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי זירא was unsure. A ברייתא forbids floating in a pool full of water, so רבי אבהו surely did not lift his feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that he did not lift his feet, for it was taught in a ברייתא: A person may not float in a pool full of water, even if it stands in a courtyard!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא's doubt. Since swimming is forbidden, רבי אבהו certainly would not have done it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא forbids floating even in a pool inside a courtyard. That is a place where one might think there is no reason to worry. So what is there to wonder about? רבי אבהו surely kept his feet down.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It is obvious that he did not lift his feet, for it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יָשׁוּט אָדָם בִּבְרֵיכָה מְלֵאָה מַיִם,
phrases.english: A person may not float in a pool full of water,
even if it stands in a courtyard!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the doubt raised in Step 31
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's uncertainty about whether רבי אבהו lifted his feet
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא clearly forbids floating, so there should be no doubt that רבי אבהו kept his feet down.

steps.title: Beginning of the answer: two different cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer with "it is not difficult" and starts to separate two cases. The rest of the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This (ברייתא is talking about a place)...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to answer the challenge in Step 32 by splitting the cases. This line is only the opening of the answer, which continues on the next part of the דף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "לא קשיא, הא" means the גמרא will show that the ברייתא and the bath of רבי אבהו are about different situations. That leaves room for רבי זירא's doubt. The details come on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces an answer)
This one (used to split between two cases)

phrases.english: It is not difficult; this (baraita refers to a place)...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge in Step 32
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting into two different cases (continues on the next amud)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא forbids all floating, so רבי אבהו surely did not lift his feet.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא refers to one kind of place, which leaves room for doubt about another (completed on the next amud).
